path_decisions.rationale: Need to verify how min_conditions interacts with backtest engine bugs (long-only, profit_target_exit SHORT bug) that prevent measuring actual condition threshold impact
Condition count is computed but never mapped to signal strength; BacktestEngine long-only + SHORT profit_target bug means short-side entry signals are wasted or mismeasured
Hardcoded strength = flat position sizing regardless of condition quality; trailing stop is the exit-side equivalent (tracks CLOSE not HIGH, no SHORT trailing stop, YAML/code multiplier mismatch)

evidence: quantflow/strategy/templates/trend_following.py:164-167: entry = int(trend_up) + int(rsi < overbought) + int(vol_ok) + int(atr_ok) >= min_conditions(4) — ALL 4 conditions required simultaneously
quantflow/strategy/templates/mean_reversion.py:99: long_count = int(vol_ok) + int(rsi < oversold) + int(close < bb_lower) — vol_ok always True at threshold 0.8, effective min_conditions = 1 of 2
quantflow/strategy/templates/volatility_breakout.py:205-208: long_count = 5 conditions (atr_spike + bb_expanding + close > bb_upper + vol_surge + previous_squeeze), min_conditions=5 requires ALL 5

quantflow/strategy/templates/_runtime.py:131-172: profit_target_exit() line 167 target_price = entry_price * (1.0 + profit_take_pct), line 169 check close >= target_price — LONG only, no SHORT handling
quantflow/strategy/research/backtest.py:60-63: BacktestEngine documented long-only; line 112 entry_values[prev_idx] enters LONG only
quantflow/strategy/templates/trend_following.py:116-122: exit_ emits Direction.SHORT with strength=0.5 — opens new SHORT position instead of closing LONG (Direction.FLAT needed)
quantflow/strategy/templates/trend_following.py:110-111: entry always emits Direction.LONG with strength=0.8 hardcoded — never varies with condition count
quantflow/strategy/templates/mean_reversion.py:69: strength=0.7 hardcoded for entry, line 77 strength=0.3 hardcoded for exit — no condition-to-strength mapping
quantflow/strategy/templates/trend_following.py:260-262: rsi_at_entry = rsi[entries].mean() — uses global mean of ALL entry bars, not per-entry RSI; with 100+ entries converges to ~50
quantflow/strategy/templates/trend_following.py:287: highest.iloc[i] = max(close[i], highest[i-1]) — tracks highest CLOSE not HIGH, premature exits on valid pullbacks
quantflow/strategy/templates/trend_following.py:292: trailing_exits = close < highest - trailing_atr * 3.0 — YAML says trailing_stop_atr_multiplier=1.5 but code defaults to 3.0
quantflow/strategy/templates/volatility_breakout.py:391: same CLOSE-not-HIGH tracking as trend_following — both strategies have premature trailing stop exits
quantflow/strategy/engine.py:91: allocation = {s.name: 1.0/len(self._strategies) for s in self._strategies} — equal 1/N allocation regardless of strategy performance
quantflow/strategy/engine.py:54: RiskEngine(config.risk) — no strategy_risk_budgets passed; line 55 PositionSizer(method='kelly') — no strategy_win_rates passed
quantflow/strategy/engine.py:150-155: flush_signals() goes directly to _process_signal(), consolidate_signals() never called — conflicting strategies can open opposing positions

candidate_solution.summary: 5-priority fix plan mapping condition count to entry strength, fixing exit direction, separating entry/exit min_conditions, fixing SHORT profit_target, and wiring YAML params to code

priority_1_critical.impact: Currently opens new SHORT instead of closing LONG — every exit creates an unwanted opposing position
priority_1_critical.code_change: Change line 118 from Direction.SHORT to Direction.FLAT

priority_2_critical.impact: SHORT positions never hit profit target — target line 167 always computes entry*(1+pct), never entry*(1-pct)
priority_2_critical.code_change: Add direction parameter; for SHORT: target_price = entry_price * (1.0 - profit_take_pct), exit when close <= target_price

priority_3_high.fix: Map condition_count to signal strength dynamically
priority_3_high.impact: All 6 templates use hardcoded strength (0.7-0.8) regardless of condition quality; PositionSizer.size() line 69 scales by strength, so weak signals get same sizing as strong ones

mapping.trend_following: min_conditions=4 total=4 → strength = 0.4 + 0.125 * conditions_met (4/4=0.9, 3/4=0.775 still enters)
mapping.mean_reversion: min_conditions=2 total=3 → strength = 0.3 + 0.2 * conditions_met (2/3=0.7, 3/3=0.9); raise vol_threshold to 1.2 per YAML
mapping.volatility_breakout: min_conditions=3 total=5 → strength = 0.2 + 0.14 * conditions_met (3/5=0.62, 5/5=0.9); lower min_conditions from 5 to 3

priority_4_high.fix: Separate entry vs exit min_conditions and remove vol_ok from exits
priority_4_high.impact: Exit requires same vol_ok as entry (line 169 trend_following) — reversals happen on LOW volume, delaying exits; mean_reversion exit at line 107-109 has no condition count at all
priority_4_high.code_change: Add exit_min_conditions param (default 2 for trend, 1 for mean_rev); exclude vol_ok from exit condition count

priority_5_high.fix: Fix trailing stop: track HIGH not CLOSE, add SHORT support, fix YAML/code mismatch
priority_5_high.impact: Using close instead of high causes premature exits on valid pullbacks; trend_following mult=3.0 vs YAML 1.5; no trailing stop for SHORT positions; mean_reversion has no trailing stop at all
priority_5_high.code_change: Track highest HIGH for LONG trailing, lowest LOW for SHORT trailing; use trailing_stop_atr_multiplier from YAML; add trailing stop to mean_reversion

interaction_effects: Condition-to-strength mapping × PositionSizer: strength currently unused for position sizing because it's always 0.7-0.8; mapping creates differentiation that Kelly sizing can exploit
Separate exit min_conditions × vol_ok: removing vol_ok from exits directly contradicts trend_following.py:168-170 where exit includes vol_ok; must choose one
vol_breakout min_conditions=5 → 3 × signal strength: lowering threshold increases entry count but also increases weak-signal entries; strength mapping counteracts this by sizing down weak entries

RSI-adaptive profit targets use global mean (rsi[entries].mean()) not per-entry RSI — with 100+ entries this converges to ~50, making the feature dead code; fix: use per-entry RSI stored at entry time

notes: Key new finding not in prior iterations: trend_following.py:118 exit emits Direction.SHORT instead of Direction.FLAT — this means every LONG exit opens a new SHORT position rather than closing the LONG. Combined with long-only BacktestEngine, this is invisible in backtest but catastrophic in paper/live. Also: mean_reversion has NO trailing stop at all — only profit_target_exit and max_holding_bars, which means winning mean-reversion trades have no mechanism to lock in gains during the hold period. The RSI-adaptive profit target feature is effectively dead code because it uses rsi[entries].mean() (global average of all entry-bar RSIs) instead of per-entry RSI.
